model.title: Uyghur Policy Act of 2026
model.meta: Foreign Relations Committee · Sen. John Curtis (R-UT)

summary.text: The bill would express the sense of Congress that China should protect the distinct ethnic, cultural, religious and linguistic identity of Uyghurs and other minority groups in Xinjiang, end detentions and transnational repression, allow access by the press, international organizations and foreign delegations, and release prisoners held for their identities or beliefs. It would require the Secretary of State to take actions supporting Uyghurs, including promoting their rights with partner countries, pressing China to close detention facilities, and tracking transnational repression, and to report to Congress within 180 days and annually for three years, with the requirements ending after five years. It would also allow the State Department to provide Uyghur language training and staff certain posts, require a report on those steps within one year, direct the U.S. United Nations representative to oppose efforts to block discussion of Xinjiang abuses and to support a special rapporteur for the region, and authorize no additional funds.
